logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF and NYHA class II to III symptoms, the use of ARNi (sacubitril-valsartan) is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF and NYHA class II to III symptoms, the use of ARNi is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality.

logic_node.action: Prescribe ACEi when ARNi not feasible
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with previous or current symptoms of chronic HFrEF, the use of ACEi is beneficial to reduce morbidity and mortality when the use of ARNi is not feasible.

source_text: In patients with previous or current symptoms of chronic HFrEF, the use of ACEi is beneficial to reduce morbidity and mortality when the use of ARNi is not feasible.

logic_node.action: Prescribe ARB when ACEi intolerant and ARNi not feasible
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with previous or current symptoms of chronic HFrEF who are intolerant to ACEi because of cough or angioedema and when the use of ARNi is not feasible, the use of ARB is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality.

source_text: In patients with previous or current symptoms of chronic HFrEF who are intolerant to ACEi because of cough or angioedema and when the use of ARNi is not feasible, the use of ARB is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality.

logic_node.action: Use ACEi or ARB for high economic value when ARNi not feasible
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with previous or current symptoms of chronic HFrEF, in whom ARNi is not feasible, treatment with an ACEi or ARB provides high economic value.

source_text: In patients with previous or current symptoms of chronic HFrEF, in whom ARNi is not feasible, treatment with an ACEi or ARB provides high economic value.

logic_node.action: Switch from ACEi or ARB to ARNi
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with chronic symptomatic HFrEF NYHA class II or III who tolerate an ACEi or ARB, replacement by an ARNi is recommended to further reduce morbidity and mortality.

source_text: In patients with chronic symptomatic HFrEF NYHA class II or III who tolerate an ACEi or ARB, replacement by an ARNi is recommended to further reduce morbidity and mortality.

logic_node.action: Prefer ARNi over ACEi for high economic value
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with chronic symptomatic HFrEF, treatment with an ARNi instead of an ACEi provides high economic value.

source_text: In patients with chronic symptomatic HFrEF, treatment with an ARNi instead of an ACEi provides high economic value.

logic_node.action: Do not co-administer ARNi with ACEi
logic_node.action_detail: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi. Concomitant use can lead to angioedema.

source_text: ARNi should not be administered concomitantly with ACEi or within 36 hours of the last dose of an ACEi.

logic_node.action: Do not administer ARNi in patients with history of angioedema
logic_node.action_detail: ARNi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema due to concern for increased risk of recurrence.

source_text: ARNi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema.

logic_node.action: Do not administer ACEi in patients with history of angioedema
logic_node.action_detail: ACEi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema. ARB do not interfere as directly with bradykinin metabolism and may be considered as an alternative.

source_text: ACEi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema.

logic_node.action: Start ACEi at low dose and titrate upward
logic_node.action_detail: ACEi should be started at low doses and titrated upward to doses shown to reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in clinical trials. Give with caution if low systemic blood pressure, renal insufficiency, or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L). If maximal doses not tolerated, use intermediate doses; avoid abrupt withdrawal.

source_text: ACEi should be started at low doses and titrated upward to doses shown to reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in clinical trials.

logic_node.action: Start ARB at low dose and titrate upward
logic_node.action_detail: ARB should be started at low doses and titrated upward, with an attempt to use doses shown to reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in clinical trials. Give with caution if low systemic blood pressure, renal insufficiency, or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L).

source_text: ARB should be started at low doses and titrated upward, with an attempt to use doses shown to reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in clinical trials.

logic_node.action: Allow 36-hour washout between ACEi and ARNi
logic_node.action_detail: If patients are switched from an ACEi to an ARNi or vice versa, there should be at least 36 hours between ACEi and ARNi doses to reduce risk of angioedema.

source_text: If patients are switched from an ACEi to an ARNi or vice versa, there should be at least 36 hours between ACEi and ARNi doses.

logic_node.action: Initiate ARNi de novo before hospital discharge for acute HF
logic_node.action_detail: ARNi should be initiated de novo in patients hospitalized with acute HFrEF before discharge in the absence of contraindications, given improvement in health status, reduction in NT-proBNP, and improvement of LV remodeling parameters compared with ACEi/ARB.

source_text: ARNi should be initiated de novo in patients hospitalized with acute HFrEF before discharge in the absence of contraindications.

logic_node.action: Monitor blood pressure, renal function, and potassium with RAS inhibitors
logic_node.action_detail: ACEi and ARB should be given with caution to patients with low systemic blood pressure, renal insufficiency, or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L). ARNi is more frequently associated with symptomatic hypotension.

source_text: ACEi and ARB should be given with caution to patients with low systemic blood pressure, renal insufficiency, or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L).
